reasoning_content: Need to find where select's value gets clobbered. The block effect runs, then effect for select runs: select_option(select, prev.value) — prev.value is undefined (no value in spread), so select_option with undefined value likely resets selection, clearing selected attribute default. In real svelte, select_option with undefined shouldn't reset... Let's look at select_option.

function.arguments: {"hypotheses":[{"claim": "In attribute_effect, the trailing select effect calls select_option(select, prev.value) without mounting=true; when the spread has no 'value', undefined matches no option and selectedIndex is set to -1, wiping the selected-attribute default.", "evidence_refs": ["packages/svelte/src/internal/client/dom/elements/attributes.js:515-520", "packages/svelte/src/internal/client/dom/elements/bindings/select.js:42-44 (!mounting || value !== undefined -> selectedIndex = -1)"], "prediction": "Passing mounting=true (as upstream does) preserves the HTML selected default when no value prop exists, and only spread selects are affected (control select has no attribute_effect).", "falsifier": "If the value is applied before options exist or timing is the issue, mounting=true will still leave selects[1].value empty."}, {"claim": "The bug is in set_attributes resetting select state, not the follow-up effect.", "evidence_refs": ["packages/svelte/src/internal/client/dom/elements/attributes.js:485-520"], "prediction": "The failure would occur even if the trailing effect were removed entirely.", "falsifier": "Removing the trailing select effect would fix the repro; if it doesn't, set_attributes is at fault."}]}
